Playbook.name: Correlation — Script Interpreter Download/Exec then External Connection - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A script interpreter downloaded/executed content and then made an external connection within 15 minutes (EQL sequence, same process). Triage: a malware download-then-C2 chain, or a legitimate script fetching a resource then calling an API?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Script download-then-external-connection is the download-cradle-then-C2 pattern of second-stage malware.

Assets.AssetType: Correlated across all JCB detection surfaces

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Sysmon process + network (event.code 3) (verified). EQL sequence rule; this playbook confirms the download and the external connection.

Signal.Name: Script Interpreter Download/Exec then Ex
Signal.Details: interpreter download/exec then external connection (same process).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Confirm the download-then-external-connection sequence and whether the destination is malicious.

Step.name: The interpreter's download and connection
Step.Purpose: The interpreter command and the external destination reveal a malware cradle vs a legitimate API call.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("1","4688") AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(powershell|pwsh|python|wscript|cscript|mshta|node).*" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE cl LIKE "*download*" OR cl LIKE "*http*" OR cl LIKE "*iex*" OR cl LIKE "*invoke*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A download cradle (IEX/DownloadString) then a connection to a suspicious external destination = malware C2. A legitimate script fetching from an internal/vendor API is benign. Read the destination.

Step.name: External connections from the host's interpreters
Step.Purpose: The external destinations the interpreter connected to determine malicious vs benign.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "3" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(powershell|pwsh|python|wscript|cscript|mshta|node).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS conns = COUNT(*), destinations = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), dest_ports = VALUES(destination.port) BY process.name | SORT conns DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Connections to a raw IP / unusual port / suspicious domain after the download = C2. Internal/vendor API endpoints = benign.

Node.Condition: A download cradle then a connection to a suspicious external destination.
A legitimate script fetching from an internal/vendor API then calling it.
A deployment/automation script downloading then connecting benignly.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-CORRSCRIPT-SEQ, INV-02-CORRSCRIPT-CONN to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate script fetching/calling an internal/vendor API.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the script/destination; close as false_positive.
Isolate the host; capture the downloaded payload; open IR; block the destination; hunt peers.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture the payload; block the destination.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate host; capture payload; block destination; open IR; hunt peers.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restrict interpreter egress; app-control on script interpreters; EDR.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the download and connection are the SAME process, and the destination is external/suspicious.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Payload captured; destination blocked; peers hunted.
